what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 2: A clock field that follows the records late: does block 95's pair law survive, and does a record trap itself?. SETTING (the moving-records column of the admissibility induced-law campaign, under the owner's reading: records move, one per site at a time; possibility shifts at the site as the neighbourhood changes; open PRs #8860 (block 95, records on their own clocks attract with a 1/r potential equal both ways) #8866 (block 96, waves need a coupling time reversal flips) #8872 (block 97, the sign: a record that cannot read the field from its own motion hops on its own clock) #8878 (block 98, a wave passing a record turns by twice the pair energy); the clock clause #8568 (block 53, with its 2026-09-23 corrigendum on the mean velocity), the walk #8570 (block 54), the kept books #8571 (block 55), the delay #8578 (block 57); decision record #8572 (tenth to thirteenth addenda); ALL clauses supplied, nothing adopted; read the relevant notes on their PR branches before starting - git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). TASK: block 95 assumes the clock field follows the records at once (P4): log w = 6 log(kappa) sum_r G(z - r), and then departure-timed hopping is in detailed balance with W(C) exp(6 log(kappa) sum_pairs G). Let the field relax instead: du_z/dt = Gamma w_z ((1/6) sum_e u_(z+e) - u_z + log(kappa)(n_z - nbar)) (the local clock times the relaxation; block 57 shows nearest-neighbour KINETIC terms carry no delay, so this first-order relaxation is a separate supplied clause). (a) For one record on a ring or torus: its effective hop rate (or diffusion constant) in the stationary state of the joint (record, field) process, exactly or to first order in 1/Gamma - does it trap itself on its own trail (sites it has visited keep slow clocks)? (b) For two records: the first-order correction to the pair law in 1/Gamma; is the joint process reversible for any finite Gamma? HIT: (a) or (b) exact, or an exact proof that no joint law of product form is stationary.
